title: layer-group Mirror views
hypothesis: Group size 2 with learned within-group Givens views will recover a teacher made from four shared layer-group bases, at materially fewer serialized bytes than untied layers and better quality than hard group tying; group size 4 will expose the quality-storage tradeoff.
physical_object: One 8x8 block per layer group, reused by two or four logical depths
mirror_coordinate: One learned Givens angle per logical layer within each group
logical_multiplicity: Eight logical depth maps from two or four physical blocks
controls: hard tying at group sizes 2 and 4
rank-1 per-layer residual on group-size-2 bases

development.selection_metric: all-layer held-out MSE after 600 Adam updates at LR 0.01

success_gate: On aligned fresh worlds, mirror2 MSE <=1.10x untied in all 3 worlds and <=1.10x the best group-size-2 non-Mirror shared control; mirror2 payload <=0.65x untied. Report mirror4 as a group-size tradeoff and independent matrices as a boundary.
failure_gate: Both development worlds miss either aligned quality or payload threshold, or rank-1 residual matches Mirror quality at materially lower payload/compute.
boundaries: Teacher directly follows size-2 group Givens orbit
